job.title: Engineering Manager

Our platform processes supplier connectivity, data acquisition, distribution, and booking workflows to ensure fresh, high-quality travel inventory with minimal latency in a high-traffic environment.

  • Team Leadership & Mentorship: Lead, grow, and mentor a team of engineers to deliver high-quality software while developing their careers.
  • Technical Strategy: Own the technical architecture for inventory management, ensuring scalability, resilience, and performance.
  • Backlog & Product Delivery: Own the team backlog, facilitating technical and product decisions in partnership with Architects, Designers, and Product Managers.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with cross-functional teams to improve supplier integrations, enhance data freshness, and streamline booking processes.
  • Engineering Best Practices: Champion standards for operational excellence, from CI/CD pipelines to system monitoring and incident response.
  • Hands-on Contribution: Contribute directly when needed by reviewing code, guiding system design, and tackling complex technical challenges.

What We're Looking For


  • Leadership Experience: Proven track record leading high-performing engineering teams, ideally within high-scale, distributed environments.
  • Core Technical Stack: Strong background in C# .NET (or Kotlin, Scala, or Java) with hands-on experience building cloud-native services on AWS.
  • Infrastructure & Automation: Experience using Kubernetes, Terraform, and CI/CD pipelines for scalable, automated deployments.
  • Data Processing & Architecture: Background in large-scale data processing, internet-scale real-time data workflows, transactional systems, and GraphQL / modern API-driven architectures.
  • Observability & Reliability: Strong focus on monitoring, observability, system uptime, and performance optimization.
  • Pragmatic Mindset: Balanced approach to technical debt, feature velocity, and operational stability, combined with a passion for data-driven experimentation and decision-making.

Work will include advising public sector bodies, utilities and local authorities, as well as private sector organisations, on a wide range of contentious and non-contentious procurement matters. Working across sectors, the group advise on all aspects of the procurement and contracting process. The team is also heavily involved in procurement disputes and litigation before the Irish Courts. Key Responsibilities:

  • Advising public and utility sector clients on all aspects of EU and Irish procurement law and national guidelines;
  • Supporting clients on strategic and high value projects in various sectors including energy, housing, transport and health.
  • Drafting and advising on complex procurement documentation and guiding clients through procurement processes, advising on evaluation methodologies, clarifications, debriefing and contract modifications;
  • Advising on contract drafting and negotiation;
  • Advising on Foreign Subsidies Regulation;
  • Advising private sector tenderers on bidding for public projects and contracts;
  • Advising clients (public and private) on procurement remedies and legal challenges before the Courts;
  • Delivering client training; and
  • Keeping up to date with legal developments in the procurement sphere and contributing to knowledge sharing and business development.

The Candidate
The ideal candidate will have 3-6 years’ PQE, with experience of advising on Irish and EU procurement law. You will be a highly motivated team player and have strong organisational and interpersonal skills as well as a good work ethic, energy, and enthusiasm.

We are looking for a candidate who not only is familiar with UCIT and AIFs and engaging with the Central Bank on Irish fund authorisations but who ideally also has experience with debt issuances and the relevant documents required to issue such securities.

  • Legislation and Regulation - Follow-up, analysis and implementation of new legislation or regulatory requirements impacting the Asset Manager and the funds under management (such as the UCITS Directives, AIFMD, MiFID II, EMIR, SFDR, CP86 and outsourcing requirements).
  • Fund Approvals/Amendments – Complete Central Bank and CSSF applications for new sub-funds and manage all post authorisation fund amendments with the Central Bank or the CSSF. Generally assist with the Asset Manager’s product development right from idea stage through to fully managing the new product approval process with the regulator and internal and external stakeholders;
  • Fund Documentation – Draft and maintain fund and management company documents (e.g.Prospectus, Supplements, KIIDs/KIDs and Business Plan) and other ancillary documents related to the investment funds under management;
  • Contracts - Draft and review a range of commercial contracts impacting the Asset Manager and the funds under management (such as IMAs with third party managers, investment advisory agreements and licensing agreements);
  • Transactional Documentation: Draft and review fund transactional documentation (such as ISDA Agreements, transaction confirmations, ISDA amendment agreements and give-up agreements);
  • Legal Advice – Provide practical, business-oriented legal advice on issues that arise for the Asset Manager in the context of its Irish and Luxembourg fund umbrellas and in respect of the Asset Manager’s own management company governance requirements;
  • Projects - Participation in ad-hoc regulatory and business projects;
  • Board and the Asset Manager Committee Preparation and Attendance – Assist internal stakeholders and the Company Secretary in respect of preparing and organising quarterly and ad hoc board meetings and attend to present topics as needed; and
  • Representation– Represent the Asset Manager at external conferences, industry events or fund association events.
Key requirements:
  • Qualified Irish Solicitor or a solicitor with equivalent qualification in another jurisdiction with 6+ years' post qualification experience (gained working in Ireland specifically).
  • Previous experience in investment funds is essential, with a demonstratable background in the understanding of investment strategies and subsequent drafting of fund product documentation.
  • Highly motivated, pragmatic, solutions-oriented and a real business partner.
  • Ability to conduct a thorough legal analysis of complex topics and translate this analysis into practical and succinct legal advice.
  • Commitment to high standards and forensic attention to detail.
  • Strong communication skills (oral and written) and ability to liaise with top management and other stakeholders.
  • Independent worker, with the organisational and task management skills necessary to manage a large volume of tasks and meet deadlines.
  • Ability to effectively prioritise work by understanding competing priorities and make appropriate judgments regarding relative importance.
  • Team player, offers to help colleagues and share work.
  • Familiar with MS-applications (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).

job.title: Head of Financial Institution Sales (EMEA)
job.description:
Regional Head of Financial Institution Sales – EMEA

Location: London. However, candidates based elsewhere in the UK or Europe will also be considered

The business is seeking a senior commercial leader to take ownership of Financial Institution sales and strategic partnerships across EMEA. Reporting directly to the CEO, this is a highly autonomous, hands-on role for an established commercial operator who can bring a strong network and convert relationships into significant, long-term revenue opportunities.

This is not a high-volume or lead-generation-focused sales position. The successful candidate will originate, structure and close a small number of high-value partnerships across banking, payments, fintech, treasury services, cross-border FX and, potentially, digital assets.

Key responsibilities:

  • Own the full commercial lifecycle, from origination and initial engagement through negotiation, implementation and revenue generation
  • Build and convert a regional pipeline of large Financial Institution and B2B partnerships
  • Develop senior relationships across banks, payment processors, fintechs, FX providers and large corporate treasury functions
  • Present cross-border payments, FX and payment infrastructure solutions to C-suite stakeholders
  • Lead complex commercial negotiations and structure tailored client propositions
  • Work closely with Product, Risk, Compliance and Finance to bring partnerships live
  • Take ownership of regional revenue, payment-volume and partnership-development targets
  • Represent the business as a trusted adviser within the European payments and financial services ecosystem

The successful candidate will likely have:

  • Significant senior-level experience in institutional sales, treasury sales, payments, banking, fintech or strategic partnerships
  • A strong and demonstrable network across Financial Institutions, payments, fintech or corporate treasury
  • A track record of personally originating and closing large, complex commercial partnerships
  • Strong knowledge of cross-border payments, FX, treasury services or payment infrastructure
  • Credibility when engaging and negotiating with CFOs, treasurers and other C-suite decision-makers
  • The ability to operate independently and establish a regional commercial presence
  • Exposure to stablecoins or digital assets would be beneficial but is not essential

This is initially a senior individual-contributor position, with the opportunity to play a central role in establishing and developing the organisation’s EMEA commercial presence.
